name: Coalesce
label: Hydra Head
lede: Sean Ingram and Jes Steineger came out of Kansas City's straight edge scene, broke the band up in 1996, 1999 and 2010, and keep getting named by metal bands as where they started.

eras.title: Breach was taken
eras.text: Jes Steineger, Stacy Hilt and Jim Redd started a band in January 1994, and Sean Ingram got back from Syracuse in time to sing. A Swedish band already had the name Breach, so they became Coalesce, cut an EP in a day and hit the road.

years.h: Two Amara alumni and a Loathe drummer start Breach
years.p: [[Jes Steineger|010f7911-1f05-408f-a26f-af35631b15ab]] and [[Stacy Hilt|4f8d8b03-a215-40ad-be04-94d8003f9fb5]], both late of the Krishnacore band Amara, start Breach in January 1994 with Jim Redd, who had drummed in the alternative metal band Loathe.

years.src: Wikipedia: Coalesce (band) · Machine Music: Pillars of the 90s
yt: Harvest of Maturity, live at the Fireside Bowl, Dec 4, 1997
years.h: Ingram leaves Syracuse by Easter and takes over the vocals
years.p: [[Sean Ingram|1170e906-848e-4769-8354-c3c0684511a2]] had left Kansas City on Christmas Day 1993 for Syracuse, New York, drawn by Earth Crisis and vegan straight edge. Back by Easter, he wrote lyrics for the band and took over vocals.
years.xp:
Ingram had fronted a straight edge band called Restrain. Wikipedia says he came home disillusioned with Syracuse's militant atmosphere, and that his first lyrics for the new band were for Harvest of Maturity.

He told Machine Music that after hearing Earth Crisis's All Out War he wanted to be part of the music scene, and that when he saw Steineger play he knew "something special was going on."

years.h: Sweden already has a Breach, so Kansas City becomes Coalesce
years.p: Wikipedia says the band renamed itself to avoid confusion between the two.

years.h: 002 takes one day at Red House Studios
years.p: The EP was recorded in Lawrence with producer Ed Rose, who would go on to record most of the band's catalog.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the U.K. arm of Earache Records signed Coalesce after hearing its demo, a year or so before the band first broke up.

years.h: Bloodlet and 108 take Coalesce on its first U.S. tour
years.p: The tour carried the 002 EP across the country, and the band came home with its lineup already fraying.

eras.title: Ingram out in March, back in July
eras.text: Coalesce broke up in March 1996 and re-formed in July with a new drummer. Both albums that followed, Give Them Rope and Functioning on Impatience, were cut at the same Lawrence studio with the same producer.

years.h: Ingram arrives at practice to find his replacement auditioning
years.p: In March 1996 drummer Jim Redd talked the others into dropping Ingram. [[James DeWees|24ff2fe2-c61c-4002-b717-444ffa811515]] was trying out for the vocal spot when the band folded.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts it down to personality clashes between Ingram and Redd that grew on tour. When Ingram walked into practice and found DeWees auditioning, a confrontation followed and Coalesce "disbanded altogether."

Redd did not come back when the band re-formed: he was heading to the University of Maryland in Baltimore.

yt: Live at Groove Farm, Kansas City, 1996
years.h: The man who auditioned to replace Ingram becomes the drummer
years.p: [[James DeWees|24ff2fe2-c61c-4002-b717-444ffa811515]] had come in to try out as a singer. When Coalesce re-formed in July 1996, he took the drums.
years.xp: The re-formed band put out the A Safe Place 7-inch on Edison Recordings and a split EP with Napalm Death, In Tongues We Speak, according to Wikipedia.

yt: Live at The Joint, Staten Island, June 20, 1997
years.h: Give Them Rope comes out on Edison Recordings
years.p: Eleven songs and about forty minutes of metalcore, recorded at Red House with Ed Rose. Fans still treat it as the band's first peak.

years.h: Coalesce splits a 7-inch with [[The Get Up Kids|1b54e90c-638e-4fdd-a20e-4ab09db9fdaf]]
years.p: Around the same time the band shared splits with Today Is the Day and Converge.

yt: 73-C, live at the Fireside Bowl, Chicago, Dec 4, 1997
years.h: Stacy Hilt quits, worn out by the shows
years.p: Wikipedia says the band's live shows had exhausted him. [[Nathan Ellis|c5ef22ff-6712-4f68-9b4b-53871a6c29c4]], who had been playing guitar, moved to bass.
years.xp: Wikipedia ties the exit to a stretch of heavy touring that included a violent show in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania.

years.h: Functioning on Impatience arrives with a rib cage on the cover
years.p: Seven songs in 20 minutes, recorded at Red House with Ed Rose and released through Second Nature Recordings. The cover photo is by Carrie Whitney.

years.h: [[Boy Sets Fire|ba561cc7-2050-47d3-8bc2-c645a1393d90]] shares the next split 7-inch
years.p: The Delaware hardcore band took the other side of a 7-inch released in the same run.

eras.title: The van dies, the debt stays
eras.text: Coalesce covered Led Zeppelin for Hydra Head, lost a tour to a broken-down van and owed Relapse a record. The record ran 24 minutes.

years.cap: Cover art directed by Aaron Turner
years.h: Coalesce covers Led Zeppelin for Hydra Head Records
years.p: Recorded in September 1998 at Red House and released by Aaron Turner's label. Steineger says it was a way to connect with his father, a [[Led Zeppelin|678d88b2-87b0-403b-b63d-5da7465aecc3]] fan.

years.src: Wikipedia: Coalesce (band) · Machine Music: Pillars of the 90s
years.h: A dead van ends the tour, and the band, again
years.p: Wikipedia and Machine Music say a tour with [[Neurosis|a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed]] and others ended on a broken-down van. Relapse had advanced the money for it, so the band owed the label a record.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's account is that the tour ran the East Coast with Neurosis, Nile and The Dillinger Escape Plan, and that the band went home in a U-Haul and broke up. Its album article puts the breakdown on a West Coast run in Idaho. Ingram told Machine Music the advance left Coalesce owing Relapse about $6,000.

After Steineger left the Hare Krishna movement the band signed to Relapse Records, and turned down an offer from the Christian label Solid State because the band was too volatile.

years.big: I gave you the money so you're gonna have to give me a record.
q: I gave you the money so you're gonna have to give me a record.
years.src: Machine Music: Pillars of the 90s · Wikipedia: Coalesce (band)
years.h: Relapse wants a record, and Coalesce isn't speaking
years.p: Ingram says Relapse president Matt Jacobson phoned after the $6,000 van advance. Ingram and Steineger weren't on speaking terms.
years.xp: Ingram recalls Steineger's answer as, roughly, "Fine, fuck it, we'll write a record." The music for 0:12 Revolution in Just Listening was written without Ingram, who came in later to record vocals on his own. Steineger worked out his guitar parts on an acoustic in about three days, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: 0:12 Revolution in Just Listening pays off the Relapse debt
years.p: Twenty-four minutes, cut at Red House with Ed Rose and released November 16, 1999. Decibel put it in its Hall of Fame in 2008.

eras.title: The internet remembers
eras.text: The band was dead and fans kept trading the records. Ingram sang for Dillinger for a night, put a touring band together and went back into the old tapes.

years.h: Ingram fills in for The Dillinger Escape Plan at Krazy Fest 4
years.p: Sean Ingram sang on July 28, 2001 in place of the vocalist who had just left Dillinger, according to Wikipedia.

years.big: To Jes it was just a band, to me it was my life.
q: To Jes it was just a band, to me it was my life.
years.h: Ingram tours as Coalesce without Steineger
years.p: Web interest surged, so [[Sean Ingram|1170e906-848e-4769-8354-c3c0684511a2]] organized a 2002 tour with Cory White of The Esoteric on guitar. He says he regretted not waiting for Jes Steineger.
years.xp: Machine Music lists Stacy Hilt on bass and James DeWees on drums for the tour, with White on guitar. Looking back, Ingram told the site: "Coalesce is, for all his faults, Jes's band."

years.src: NPR: A Tale Of Two Ropes
years.h: Edison Recordings reissues Give Them Rope as Give Them Rope, She Said
years.p: The remastered, remixed version came with new artwork, after the band spent 2002 to 2004 reworking the album.
years.xp: Ingram told NPR the rework was hands-on: "we chopped songs, we added different parts in, we altered vocals." He credited producer Ed Rose with working through it alongside the band.

eras.title: Back because they wanted to
eras.text: A Hellfest booking got Steineger to say yes. Coalesce came back with a new drummer, a 7-inch and Ox on Relapse, then took another break.

years.src: Scene Point Blank interview · Wikipedia: Coalesce (band)
years.h: Hellfest collapses, so Coalesce plays two clubs instead
years.p: The Trenton, NJ festival fell through over legal problems. With Steineger back and Nathan Richardson on drums, the band played venues in Philadelphia and the Wilkes-Barre area.
years.xp:
Steineger told Scene Point Blank that Hellfest organizer Dan Askew contacted him in 2005 with an offer. Seeing quite a few reunions on the bill, he figured Coalesce could play it as a retro act, and his life had reached the stability he wanted when he left in 1999, so "it seemed like a fun thing to do."

Wikipedia adds that Coalesce played what it called a final show in Lawrence that September, and that Ingram talked about writing new music under a new name, a plan that was dropped.

years.cap: Jes Steineger and Sean Ingram at Fest 8, Gainesville, Florida
years.src: Scene Point Blank interview · Wikipedia: Coalesce (band)
years.h: Salt and Passage puts the first new songs in eight years on a 7-inch
years.p: "Son of Son of Man" and "I Am This," recorded at Black Lodge Studios and released September 11, 2007 in a hand-screened gatefold cover.
years.xp: Steineger told Scene Point Blank that working with Ed Rose was "so nice to do" and that the record captured what Coalesce was between 2005 and 2007. Wikipedia notes a companion DVD, No Business in this Business, came out the same month.

years.cap: Coalesce at the Triple Rock, Minneapolis, April 25, 2009
years.src: Wikipedia: Coalesce (band) · Scene Point Blank interview
years.h: Ten years on, Ox arrives with bluegrass in it
years.p: Recorded at Black Lodge in early 2009, produced by Ed Rose, and released by Relapse on June 9. It leans on Americana and Spaghetti Westerns, per Wikipedia, and reached No. 28 on the Top Heatseekers chart.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Gillian Welch, Nickel Creek and Bill Monroe among the touchstones Steineger and Ellis brought to the record. Richardson played drums, and an EP, OXEP, followed that November.

Steineger told Scene Point Blank the point was doing it themselves: "Coalesce doesn't need some outside entity to fund it anymore."

years.cap: Sean Ingram with a megaphone, March 8, 2010
years.h: A year after Ox, Coalesce says it's stopping for now
years.p: The June 18, 2010 statement said the members wanted to focus on their personal lives, according to Wikipedia.

years.big: I'm trying to un-Lucas-ify this thing as much as possible.
q: I'm trying to un-Lucas-ify this thing as much as possible.
years.src: NPR: A Tale Of Two Ropes · Machine Music: Pillars of the 90s
years.h: Ingram finds the 1997 tapes in his basement
years.p: Relapse's two-disc Give Them Rope sets the 1997 mix next to the 2004 remix and restores the original title.
years.xp:
Ingram told NPR that the original masters were gone: "All I had for the 1997 record was just the original DAT tapes that were literally in my basement."

Looking back in 2021 he told Machine Music what he took from the remix: "Let the fuck-up be, leave it alone, don't try to fix it."

years.h: After the Granada, twelve years of quiet
years.p: On October 20, 2012 Coalesce played Lawrence's Granada Theatre on a bill with Converge, Torche and Kvelertak. It was the band's last show until 2024, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: Back for Furnace Fest, then a hard January
eras.text: Twelve years after the Granada, Coalesce returned for a festival and a hometown show with a new drummer. In January 2026 the guitarist stepped down and the European dates were canceled.

years.h: Furnace Fest brings Coalesce back after twelve years
years.p: The February announcement was followed on September 7 by a hometown show opening for Chat Pile in Lawrence, with Jeff Gensterblum on drums, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Steineger steps down, and Europe and Roadburn are off
years.p: Stereogum reported allegations from a former student at the university where he taught, and Steineger said he was stepping down. The band canceled its European dates.
years.xp:
Stereogum reported that the allegations surfaced in a Reddit thread in December 2025, describing an inappropriate email exchange between Steineger, then teaching at Lindenwood University, and a former student and advisee. The band first said, "After reviewing the evidence ourselves, we stand behind Jes," and the former student disputed that account online.

Steineger later wrote that "public attention surrounding my personal failures has become too heavy a burden."

sources.title: NPR: A Tale Of Two Ropes
